sections.h2: What has to happen before an Elmhurst house can close?
sections.html:
Elmhurst requires a passed sump pump inspection and a purchased transfer stamp before a sale inside city limits can close, and those two steps control the timeline more than anything else. The city says it requires a sump pump inspection for every residential and commercial property prior to closing, with some exceptions for condo complexes. A sale of a house in Elmhurst therefore starts with a phone call to the city, well ahead of the contract date.

  • Book the sump pump inspection at least two weeks before closing, because same-week slots are rare.
  • Submit the transfer stamp application on the city's online portal.
  • Settle every city account: utilities, inspection fees, building permit fees, fines and parking tickets.
  • Have the signed sales contract, the deed and the state MyDec declaration ready before the stamp is issued.

Addresses in unincorporated Elmhurst, which include a letter in the street number such as 16W212, do not need the city sump inspection or the city stamp.

sections.h2: What does the Elmhurst sump pump inspection check?
sections.html:
The inspection checks that the pit has a cover and that only stormwater drains to it. Bathrooms, washers and utility sinks may not drain into a storm pit. If the pump discharges overland, it must drain toward the middle of the front or back of the lot and cannot reach a neighbor's yard, the city sidewalk or the parkway. If it drains underground, it must connect to the storm sewer and never the sanitary sewer, since a sanitary connection counts as illegal.

A passing result earns a certificate of compliance on site, and an approved inspection is good for six months. A failed inspection means repairing the problem and rebooking before stamps are issued, and the city says it will not accept a legal letter in place of a pass. Someone over 18 must be present, and the city asks you not to leave inspection requests on voicemail. The number is (630) 530-3030. An inspection done through RJN does not count.

Flooding is part of the local background: the city has tended to flood after large rainfalls and is working on mitigation. A 59-acre quarry west of downtown holds stormwater, and a tunnel from Salt Creek diverts water into it during floods.

sections.h2: How much is the Elmhurst transfer stamp?
sections.html:
For most sales, the stamp costs $1.50 per $1,000 of the sale price, rounded to the nearest thousand, and the seller is responsible for buying it. The city wants all information five business days before it issues the stamp. You apply through the online portal, and the application asks for the property address, owner and buyer names, closing and move-out dates, the full consideration and the seller's forwarding address.

Beginning January 1, 2026, exempt transfers also need a stamp. Examples the city lists include adding or removing a name after marriage or divorce, transfers to or from a trust, foreclosure or short sale, transfers with governmental bodies, and transfers with consideration under $100. The exempt stamp has a $30 administrative fee, and it requires a sump pump inspection if none was done in the last five years. A signed and notarized deed goes with the application.

City Hall's finance counter issues stamps Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., or the city can mail one if you attach a prepaid shipping label. Payment options are online by card or e-check, or in person by cash, check or card. Questions go to the finance department at 630-530-3117 or 3118.

sections.h2: Can I get an Elmhurst transfer tax refund?
sections.html:
Yes, in one situation. Under the Elmhurst Municipal Code, the payor of the tax can receive a refund if they previously owned and lived in an Elmhurst home and, within 180 days of that closing, buy and occupy a new residence in Elmhurst. The city posts a Transfer Stamp Refund Form on its transfer stamp page.

This helps local move-up and downsizing sellers, who sell one Elmhurst home and buy another. Keep proof of both closings and both periods of occupancy. If you plan to leave the city, no refund applies.

sections.h2: What happens with the final water reading and trash cans?
sections.html:
Once your sump pump inspection is approved and the stamp form is in, the city pulls your current and forwarding address information and sets the final water reading itself. You do not call to schedule it. The reading happens on the day of closing, and the final bill goes to the forwarding address listed on the transfer stamp request.

Garbage, sewer and water share one bill, so the city says there is nothing extra to arrange for those services. The trash and recycling carts belong with the address, so leave them for the buyer.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Elmhurst homes?
sections.html:
Elmhurst is a western suburb in DuPage and Cook counties with 46,111 residents estimated for July 1, 2025. The owner-occupied rate was 79.9 percent for 2020 to 2024, and the median value of an owner-occupied home was $545,400. Median household income reached $149,644, and 64.2 percent of adults 25 and over held a bachelor's degree or higher.

sections.h2: Which schools, transit and history shape Elmhurst listings?
sections.html:
Elmhurst Community Unit School District 205 serves most of the city, and its high school is York Community High School. Villa Park District 45, Salt Creek District 48 and Hillside District 93 serve other parts, feeding into DuPage High School District 88 or Proviso West. Elmhurst University, a four-year liberal arts college, is also in the city.

The Metra Union Pacific West Line stops at the Elmhurst station, Pace buses run through town, and O'Hare is about 18 minutes away. The community began as Cottage Hill in 1845, took the Elmhurst name in 1869 and incorporated as a village in 1882. Several homes were designed by Mies van der Rohe, Frank Lloyd Wright and Walter Burley Griffin, which can set a house apart in a listing.

Deeds go to the DuPage County Recorder or the Cook County Clerk. DuPage's Recorder holds records going back to 1839, and Cook prices a deed at $107 on its schedule effective April 1, 2024, with state transfer tax at .50 per $500 and county tax at .25 per $500.

faqs.q: Do I need a sump pump inspection to sell in Elmhurst?
faqs.a: Yes, for properties inside city limits. The city requires an approved inspection before it issues transfer stamps, with some exceptions for condominium complexes. Schedule it at least two weeks before closing, since same-week openings are unlikely.

faqs.q: How long is an Elmhurst sump pump certificate valid?
faqs.a: An approved inspection is good for six months, and the certificate shows its expiration date. Bring it to the City Hall finance counter when you collect your transfer stamps.

faqs.q: What is the Elmhurst transfer stamp rate?
faqs.a: The city lists $1.50 per $1,000 of the sale price, rounded to the nearest thousand, for non-exempt sales. Exempt transfers carry a $30 administrative fee. The seller is responsible for buying the stamp.

faqs.q: Is Elmhurst's sump rule the same in unincorporated areas?
faqs.a: No. The city says a sump inspection and city stamps do not apply to unincorporated Elmhurst addresses, which show a letter in the street number such as 16W212. Check your address before you book.

faqs.q: Who pays for the final water reading in Elmhurst?
faqs.a: The city schedules the reading for the day of closing once your inspection is approved and your stamp form is filed. Your final bill goes to the forwarding address you list. Garbage, water and sewer share one bill, so there is nothing extra to arrange.
